chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). A man entered, greeted, and he (peace be upon him) asked him: 'How are those from your brothers whom you left behind?' He said, 'They praised well, were praised, and extolled.' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'How is the visiting/consolation of their rich ones towards their poor ones?' He said, 'Little.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And how is the observation/consideration of their rich ones towards their poor ones?' He said, 'Little.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how is the connection/relating of their rich ones to their poor ones with regards to what is in their hands?' He said, 'You are mentioning manners; little is what it is among those in our presence.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how do you claim about them that they are Shia?'

key_terms.عِيَادَةُ: Visiting/consolation (often used for sick or poor)

ai.seo_question: What criteria does Imam al-Sadiq use to evaluate the authenticity of Shia social relations?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the superficiality of the early Shia community by contrasting their verbal praise with their neglect of material and social support for the poor. He argues that true 'Shi'a' identity is defined not merely by theological affiliation but by the tangible fulfillment of rights (*huquq*) between rich and poor, a core tenet of Shia social ethics. This narrative underscores the practical dimension of faith, where economic solidarity serves as the primary metric for validating communal belonging.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and a man came over. So he greeted, and he<sup>asws</sup> asked him: ‘How are the ones from your brethren whom you left behind?’ So he praised them well, and admired them. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘How is the consolation of their rich ones upon their poor ones’. So he said, ‘Little’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And how is the observation (consideration) of their rich ones to their poor ones?’ He said, ‘Little’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So how is the helping of their rich ones to their poor ones with regards to what is in their hands?’ So he said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are mentioning manners. Little is what it is among the ones in our presence’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So how did you claim about them that they are Shia?’
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan who has said the following:

“Once, I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) when a man came and offered the greeting of peace. The Imam asked, ‘How are your brothers (in belief) whom you have left behind?’ He praised, admired and extolled them. The Imam asked, ‘Do their wealthy ones visit their poor ones?’ He said, ‘It is very rare.’ The Imam asked, ‘Do their rich ones reach out to the poor ones?’ He said, ‘It is very rare.’ “The Imam asked, ‘Do their rich ones maintain good relations with their poor ones financially?’ He said, ‘You are speaking of the moral behavior that is practiced very rarely in our people.’ The narrator has said that the Imam then asked, ‘Why do you then think they are Shi’a (Muslims)?”’
